newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aristocrat says market still strong.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aristocrat says market still strong.

text.p: Gambling machine manufacturer Aristocrat Industries Ltd said on Thursday its domestic market remains strong and it had a well defined strategy to expand internationally, particularly in North America and Europe.
"The development of entertaining and innovative games is fundamental to Aristocrat's success," chairman Allan McDonald told the annual meeting.

He said that in the domestic market, the company's Mark IV range of games and a new range of games introduced for the Mark V machine had appealled to players for their entertainment value and to venue operators for the revenue premium they deliver.
"Internationally, five reel video games are proving highly successful, increasingly so in North America, as sales penetrate markets where Aristocrat is licensed," McDonald said.
"For example, initial reaction from Atlantic City, New Jersey, venues to our games has been very positive," he said.
McDonald said that as gaming becames more integrated with the leisure industry, it would drive market expansion.
"This will, we anticipate, generate opportunities for the growth and expansion of Aristocrat," he said.

McDonald said that associated with this, and an area with exciting potential for business growth, was Aristocrat's Gaming Solutions Division, which provides systems and distributes theming modules for gaming venues.
"Aristocrat has committed significant management resources to these lines of business and believes they have considerable future potential," he said.

He said that in recent months agreements had been entered into with Konami and Innovative Gaming Corporation of America to distribute some of their gaming products throughout Australia and New Zealand and these distributed products were being
submitted to gaming regulators in Australia for approval.
"With arrangements such as these, Aristocrat is continuing the expansion of its product range beyond its traditional markets and to be a broad supplier to the gaming industry."
McDonald said Aristocrat was committed to lodging a formal application to be licensed to manufacture and sell gaming devices in Nevada before the end of 1997 calendar year.

"We are advised that the process will involve thorough review and investigation by the Nevada Gaming Board of all aspects of the operation and management of Aristocrat and of individual officers and shareholders," McDonald said.

"Subsequently, a hearing will take place before the Nevada Gaming Commission at which, amont other matters, the outcome and conclusion of the Nevada Gaming Board investigations will be considered," he said.
"Access to the Nevada market is regarded as being of great importance to the future growth of Aristocrat and its ability to remain competitive," he said.

McDonald earlier told meeting the company remained confident of achieving its profit forecast for the year to June 30, 1997 contained in its prospectus, based on the first quarter resutls and present trading trends. Aristocrat forecast earnings before
tax and abnormals of A$32.8 million for the 1996/97 year.
The company reported an operating profit of A$24.08 million in 1995/96, above the prospectus forecast of A$23.7 million.
Aristocrat listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in July.
